description: Cinema mode for Minecraft: letterbox, colour grading, depth of field and a director that shoots your scenes. Fabric 1.21.6-1.21.8.

mods.name: Absolute Cinema Camera
mods.description: Turns the game into a film: letterbox bars, hidden HUD, colour grading, depth of field, smoothed camera moves and a director that flies cinematic shots around the scene – following whoever is talking on Simple Voice Chat or playing the scene out in chat. Playtested by Contik, Cmetanochkaa, Gizmons_ and Morda_, whose evening in a tavern is why the camera keeps up with a conversation at all. Thanks to tkvach for the mod icon.

releases.notes:
People in the way.

- **Passers-by fade out of the lens.** Anybody who is not part of the scene and comes close to the camera fades out, all the way to nothing against the glass, and comes back as they step away. Participants never fade, however close they stand – one of them in the foreground is a shot, not a fault. On by default, with the distance in the settings and a key to switch it on the spot.
- **A crowd still costs the shot, just later.** A wall of backs too far out to be faded is given three times as long as a wall of stone before the camera recomposes: stone will be there next second, people crossing the room will not.
- **Keys to widen and narrow the scene**, a block at a time, without opening the settings. The ring on the floor shows up for a few seconds after each change, so you can see who is in it.

Minecraft 1.21.6–1.21.8, Fabric.

releases.notes:
The height limit now decides who may take the camera, not only who is framed.

- **A conversation on another storey cannot cut the camera away.** The scene height limit used to apply to the scene alone. Who was allowed to take the frame was decided by distance, and a distance is a sphere: the sphere goes through a floor, so a table talking downstairs was well inside the twenty-four blocks and the camera left the room to film it. Standing on a first floor, or on a balcony over a street, that is most of the building.
- **Three blocks by default rather than four.** Four was a storey plus the slack to reach the next one, which let the ground floor back into a scene played on the floor above it.

The limit is asked in one place now, and by everything that can claim the camera: the scene, a voice, a line of chat. Nothing to change in the settings, though a config file written by an earlier version keeps the height it already has – the new default only applies to a fresh one.

releases.notes:
Cutting by hand.

- **A key for the angle.** Press it and the camera composes a different frame at once. Bound to F9 by default, and there is a `/cinema shot` command for it too.
- **The automatic change can be switched off.** With **Change the angle by hand** on, a frame stands until you ask for another one, instead of changing on a timer.

Only while the camera is filming the room: whoever starts speaking still takes the frame at once, since being told who has the floor is what those modes are for and no key is quicker than a voice. A shot jammed against a wall is still recomposed without asking.

In the other modes the key does whatever another angle means there – the dialogue picks a new side of the group, the side track changes flank, and the tripod does nothing, being a tripod.

releases.notes:
Follows a scene played out in text as well as in voice.

- The shot owns its angle, so nobody steers the camera with their own mouse
- No walking sway, and no crosshair
- Speaker focus splits handover from hold, and a turn has a maximum length
- Dialogue holds everyone in a master shot and cuts in to whoever speaks, instead of covering a chosen pair and dropping the rest of the table
- Chat messages and roleplay emotes count as turns, read from the tagging the server already puts on its own messages
- Everyone is fitted against the real field of view, the letterbox included
- Signs and frames in front of the lens are not drawn
- The camera comes with you when you leave the scene, keeps out of people, and can be raised or lowered by hand
- The scene has a height limit, so a tavern's upper floor is a different scene
- Settings apply as they are changed, and the scene radius is drawn in the world

Thanks to Contik, Cmetanochkaa, Gizmons_ and Morda_ for testing the mod.
